newsitem.title: FRANCE: MEPs concerned about animal transport.
newsitem.headline: MEPs concerned about animal transport.

text.p: The European Parliament on Friday demanded the swift introduction of better animal transport standards throughout the European Union.
"It is quite feasible to combine a vibrant internal and external trade in live animals without having to compromise the welfare of animals in transport," the parliament said in a resolution.

Reacting to reports of horses imported into Italy from eastern Europe under apparently appalling conditions and public concern about veal crates, the assembly said all trade which caused animals to suffer should cease immediately.

A statement from the European Commission last month said: "The substance of the complaint is that overloaded trucks with sick, injured and dead horses arrived at (three Italian) border posts and that veterinary treatment, feed, water and rest was either not provided or was totally inadequate."
The MEPs criticised the member states' failure to bring in new standards for animal transport vehicles and staging post rules by the June 1996 deadline laid down in directive 95/29/EC.
The new rules, which include guarantees that animals are fit to undertake a journey and minimum rest periods, must be in place by December 31, 1996, in all member states, the MEPs said.
They also wanted to see effective checks on animal lorries, following accusations by animal welfare groups that rules are being flouted all over Europe.
At a meeting of EU farm ministers in October, Germany said payment of EU export refunds for livestock should be made conditional on respect for the animals' welfare.
